title: Aba Women's War (Igbo Women's War)
summary: From November 1929 Igbo women in southeastern Nigeria protested against British-appointed warrant chiefs and fears of a new tax, after a dispute with a census taker at Oloko. They used song and ridicule and attacked Native Court buildings. Colonial forces killed over 50 women; the warrant chief system was replaced in 1933.

uncertainty.note: Swarthmore dates the campaign November–December 1929; the Open University page gives December 1929 to January 1930.

where.modern_name: Aba, Abia State, Nigeria (pin is Aba, the town the event is named for; protests spread over two provinces and 6,000 square miles)
where.historical_name: Aba and the Owerri and Calabar districts, British Nigeria

importance.justification: A mass women's protest that effectively ended the warrant chief system under British rule in Nigeria.

audience_note: Describes colonial troops and police shooting dead more than 50 protesting women.

The pin is the town of Aba because the Open University page names it; the first protest was at Oloko, whose OSM match is a different Nigerian village, so it is not used.
